key_insight: A geometrically exact planar beam model can incorporate hyperelasticity cleanly by separating cross-sectional kinematics from constitutive plane-stress or plane-strain reductions.
engineering_relevance: This gives a more consistent way to model beam bending and thickness changes in large-deformation simulations, especially when Poisson's ratio effects matter.
method: Start from a conventional three-field geometrically exact planar beam formulation.
Enrich the kinematics with a global in-plane thickness deformation field.
Treat the out-of-plane response independently using either plane-stress or plane-strain constitutive reduction for hyperelastic laws.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports benchmark comparisons showing plane-stress gives nearly identical centerline deformation across Poisson's ratios, while plane-strain becomes much stiffer at higher Poisson's ratios; Saint Venant-Kirchhoff and Neo-Hookean models also agree closely overall.
watch_item: Plane-strain assumptions can introduce strong Poisson's ratio sensitivity and over-stiffen the beam, so the constitutive reduction must be chosen carefully.
paper_title: On finite elements for geometrically-exact planar beams with hyperelastic material models
